clue.text: Visitors all at sea, defeated by slow bowler

definitions.text: Visitors all at sea, defeated by slow bowler

parts.words: Visitors all at sea, defeated by slow bowler
parts.note: unwelcome visitors who came by sea in 1588 and were beaten by Drake, who famously finished his game of bowls first

explanation.surface: A touring cricket side, hopelessly lost, is skittled by a spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of touring visitors and a slow bowler is the cover; the slow bowler is Sir Francis Drake, said to have finished his game of bowls before sailing against the Spanish fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish fleet sent against England in 1588 was invaders at sea, defeated by Drake's navy.

clue.text: End of mini smashed into boat

indicators.note: the car and the boat are smashed together, so their letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small Mini car crashes into a boat, ending its journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' reads as asking for a last letter, but 'End' is the definition and 'of' a link; the letters of MINI and BOAT are mixed together by 'smashed into'. A Mini is a small British car.
explanation.definitionFit: An end can mean an aim or goal, as in 'to that end', which is what a person's driving desire pursues.

clue.text: Concerned with angular function of miracle in grotto possibly?

indicators.note: the question mark and 'possibly' suggest the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Asking whether a miracle seen in a grotto might be a matter of angles.
explanation.walkthrough: A grotto miracle suggests a religious vision such as Lourdes; 'possibly' turns the letters of MIRACLE IN GROTTO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sines, cosines and tangents are functions of angles, the subject matter of that branch of mathematics.

clue.text: Pinch a bit

explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' reads as 'a little', but it is the horse's bit placed in its mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch is slang for stealing or grabbing, and a jointed mouthpiece for a horse is a type of bit.

clue.text: After Hitchcock film, his patter could turn out beneficial

definitions.text: After Hitchcock film, his patter could turn out beneficial

indicators.note: the anagram comes after the film title in the answer

parts.note: Psycho is Alfred Hitchcock's 1960 thriller

indicators.note: the words his patter could turn out differently once rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recovering after seeing a Hitchcock film finds a counsellor's chat helpful.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a talking therapist's patter is meant to prove beneficial. 'could turn out' rearranges the letters of 'his patter', and 'After' puts them behind the film title.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking therapist treats the mind, and their patter is meant to benefit a patient.

clue.text: Leg chain?

parts.note: suggests a fetter or a relay of legs, but means a decorative chain worn around the lower leg

explanation.definitionFit: A piece of jewellery worn just above the foot is a chain around the leg.

clue.text: Scandinavian sliced loaf

indicators.note: the loaf is cut up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian cuts up a loaf of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sliced' rearranges LOAF. 'Scandinavian' defines by example: it is a Norse man's name, borne by several kings of Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a traditional Norse given name, so its bearer is typically a Norwegian or other Nordic person.

clue.text: Stuff taken from hamper endlessly

indicators.note: the word for hamper loses its final letter

parts.note: to hamper is to restrict or cramp

explanation.surface: Food is taken out of a picnic hamper without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' looks like a picnic basket but is the verb, CRAMP; 'endlessly' removes its final P.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff something is to pack it tightly full.

clue.text: Manage career

explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun for a profession but is the verb meaning to hurtle.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage a business is to operate it, and to career is to rush along at speed.

clue.text: Legs in movement make one run

indicators.note: the letters of the words legs in are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricketer's legs get moving to scamper one run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in movement' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is part of the fodder LEGS IN and 'movement' signals the anagram; 'make' links. In cricket a single is one run scored.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batter scoring a solitary run off a ball is said to score this.

clue.text: Adventurous sweetheart does not take long

indicators.note: the letter for long is left out of the endearment

parts.note: darling is a term of endearment for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A bold lover does not stay long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does not take' removes L (long) from DARLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adventurous means being bold and willing to take risks.

clue.text: Restoration of features in theatre

parts.note: sounds like a revival of stage works, but means surgery in an operating theatre to rejuvenate the face

explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic surgery tightens the skin of the face, restoring youthful looks in an operating room.

clue.text: Winning it latterly? A notion to excite!

indicators.note: the words are stirred up so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who has recently won gets excited by the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to excite' stirs LATTERLY A NOTION. The definition is cryptic: winning the UK's state-run lottery game.
explanation.definitionFit: A UK draw where people buy tickets is the thing to win, the big jackpot prize.

clue.text: Routine game on square

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union, a game
a T-square is a drawing tool, so T is square

explanation.surface: A regular game is played on the village square.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is rugby union; T comes from the T-square used by draughtsmen. 'on' links, placing one after the other in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rut is a dull, fixed pattern of behaviour, a groove one cannot escape.

clue.text: City moony about the budget

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: the word moony is turned about, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreamy City figure muses on the Chancellor's Budget.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postal district of the City of London, its financial centre; 'about' shuffles MOONY. 'the' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Economy class is the cheap, low-cost option, just as budget means inexpensive.

clue.text: Cry of surprise that accompanies a bill?

definitions.text: Cry of surprise that accompanies a bill?

parts.words: Cry of surprise that accompanies a bill?
parts.note: an exclamation on seeing a big invoice, but also the soft call of a dove, which in the phrase bill and ___ goes with a beak

explanation.definitionFit: It is a British exclamation of astonishment and the murmuring sound a pigeon makes, paired with bill in the phrase for courting.

clue.text: This wine may become light at table

definitions.text: This wine may become light at table

parts.words: This wine may become light at table
parts.note: the straw-wrapped bottle of this Tuscan wine is often reused as a candle holder on restaurant tables

explanation.definitionFit: A red from Tuscany comes in the round straw-covered flask that trattorias turn into candlesticks.

clue.text: A royal touch of distinction

explanation.walkthrough: 'of' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial tap of a sword by the monarch conferring knighthood is one meaning, and an honour or award is the other.

clue.text: A writer put down

parts.note: a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A writer puts something down on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' looks like writing but means to attribute, as in putting success down to luck.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute a cause to something is to credit it to that source.

clue.text: When so broke, need hit to follow

indicators.note: the word for hit comes after the word for need

parts.note: need means want or destitution
stricken means hit or struck

explanation.surface: Someone so short of money needs a hit to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When so' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being penniless means extremely poor, with no money at all.

clue.text: Like an Arab, say, endlessly sequined

indicators.note: the word sequined loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An Arab horse wears a sequined costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' is the breed of horse, not a person; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to horses, of which the Arabian is a famous breed.

clue.text: Book three's about a queen of Persia

indicators.note: the letters of three's are turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A book about a queen of Persia counts three of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The extra phrase 'a queen of Persia' describes the biblical heroine whose book this is.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a book of the Old Testament telling of a Jewish queen of the Persian king.

clue.text: One provides a deal for the better

definitions.text: One provides a deal for the better

parts.words: One provides a deal for the better
parts.note: sounds like someone who improves things, but means a casino worker dealing cards to a person placing bets

explanation.definitionFit: A casino employee who runs the gaming table deals cards to a gambler.

clue.text: Tour abandoned in utter defeat

indicators.note: the word tour is abandoned to disorder, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A tour is abandoned after a crushing defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' shuffles TOUR; 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing loss where the beaten side flees in disorder.

clue.text: Polished top Eli renovated

indicators.note: the words top Eli are made over, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eli has polished and renovated the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polished' looks like a verb about shining, but means refined in manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Courteous and refined behaviour is described as well-mannered.

clue.text: Spanish gooseberry?

parts.note: a gooseberry is British slang for an unwanted third person with a couple; in Spain the traditional one was a chaperone

explanation.walkthrough: Playing gooseberry, in British slang, is being the awkward third person accompanying a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: An older woman acting as chaperone to young girls in a Spanish family, always present with courting pairs.

clue.text: Surgeon embraces university coach

indicators.note: the surgeon's letters wrap around the university letter

parts.note: BS stands for Bachelor of Surgery

explanation.surface: A surgeon hugs a university coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like a sports trainer but is the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a long-distance road vehicle carrying passengers.

clue.text: Achievement, however you look at it!

indicators.note: reading left to right or right to left gives the same word

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An achievement looks good from every angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is a notable act or feat.
